memoryText: The LORD is my chosen portion and my cup; you hold my lot. The lines have fallen for me in pleasant places; indeed, I have a beautiful inheritance.
readingInstruction: Today there is no new reading. This week you followed Israel through Jericho, Ai, Gibeon, and the northern campaign, and you read the long lists of tribal allotments. Today, rest in the one thing all these chapters point to: God himself is the inheritance of his people. If you have time, reread Psalm 16.
memoryVerseMeditation:
Psalm 16:5-6 takes the dry geography of this week’s reading and turns it into worship.

“The LORD is my chosen portion and my cup.” The Levites received no land, and the text said, “the LORD is their inheritance.” David says the same of himself, and the New Testament says it of every believer. If you are in Christ, you have been given God. Not just his gifts, or his help, but himself.

“You hold my lot.” A lot is something cast, and what falls is out of your hands. But David says that God holds it. Your circumstances, your family, your calling, and your seasons are not random. They are in the hand of one who loves you.

“The lines have fallen for me in pleasant places.” The boundary lines in Joshua were measured with cords. David looks at the lines of his life and calls them pleasant. This does not mean everything is easy. It means that the gift of God himself outweighs any other loss.

“Indeed, I have a beautiful inheritance.” This is a statement of gratitude. Say the verse aloud. Notice what you are tempted to compare. Then let the verse reorient you toward the one who holds you. Christ is the heir of all things, and in him you are a co-heir.
weekInReview:
This week you saw what a faithful God does with a faithful people. You listened to the music of Psalm 66, which called you to shout for joy and recalled God’s testing. You watched Jericho fall without a siege and Israel stumble at Ai because of Achan’s hidden sin. You watched Joshua make a hasty treaty with Gibeon and see the sun stand still. You followed the northern campaign and the list of defeated kings, and then read the first of the great land allotments, with Caleb asking for his mountain at eighty-five and the daughters of Zelophehad claiming their inheritance. And you sang Psalm 16, where David calls the LORD his portion and his cup.

The week held two truths together: God is holy and judges sin, and he is also faithful and gives his people an inheritance.
reflectionQuestions: Where is God calling you to trust his power instead of your own resources? Jericho fell by faith and obedience, and Ai fell after sin was dealt with. Think about a situation you are tempted to handle by effort alone. What would it look like to pray first, and then obey?

How does Jesus fulfill what Joshua only began? Joshua led Israel into a land, but the land was partial and was lost. Jesus, whose name means the same thing, leads his people into a better inheritance that cannot fade. How does Hebrews 4:8-9 or Psalm 16:10-11 help you see the difference? What does it mean to you that the inheritance is secured by Christ’s resurrection?

What are you tempted to count as your portion apart from God? Money, status, comfort, relationships, or reputation can all quietly become what we live for. Name one and ask the Lord to teach you to say, “You are my portion.”
prayerPrompts: Thank God that he is your portion and that your lines have fallen in pleasant places.
Thank Jesus, the true Joshua, for winning an inheritance you could never earn.
